newsitem.title: HONG KONG: UK reassures HK British passport holders.
newsitem.headline: UK reassures HK British passport holders.

text.p: The British-led government in Hong Kong on Wednesday sought to reassure holders of British passports in the territory that they would receive some form of consular protection after the handover next year.
But it admitted in a statement that their dual nationalities would limit Britain's ability, under international law, to provide full consular protection.
"Even if we were persuaded that he or she were a dual national, that would not in itself stop us from making representations on his or her behalf," it said.
"(But) we accept that international law limits the ability of the U.K. to provide full consular protection to dual nationals in the country or territory of their other nationality."

The statement follows remarks made on Tuesday by Britain's Senior Trade Commissioner, Francis Cornish, that London could not give consular protection to the more than 135,000 Hong Kong people granted British passports recently.
In a concession to widespread demands for full British citizenship following Beijing's 1989 Tiananmen crackdown, London offered passports to 50,000 heads of households.
Hong Kong, a British colony of over a century and a half, reverts to Chinese rule next July 1.

Cornish, whose remarks have prompted charges that Britain was not keeping to its promises, said China regarded these people as holders of dual citizenship and would not recognise British consular protection for them on Chinese soil.
The statement also said it was for Britain to decide what representation it wanted to make for the passport holder.
